papers.title_in_file: Harnessing Quantum Extreme Learning Machines for image classification
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2409.00998v3 (10 Apr 2025); the record id carries year 2025 and the file name 2024.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results discussion, conclusions and appendix B. Methods sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of a quantum extreme learning machine (quantum reservoir) for MNIST and Fashion-MNIST image classification, varying encoding, data reduction and reservoir Hamiltonian.

assertions.value: The authors report that adding a quantum reservoir systematically improves the accuracy of the image classifier.
quotes: Our results show that the introduction of a quantum reservoir systematically improves the accuracy of the classifier.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST.

assertions.value: The authors report that Hamiltonians with distinct structures exhibit the same discrimination rate, depending on how their eigenstates relate to the encoding and measurement basis.
quotes: Hamiltonians with distinct structures exhibit the same discrimination rate, depending on how their eigenstates are related to the encoding and measurement basis.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study was limited to systems with up to 12 qubits because of the computational cost of simulating quantum computers.
quotes: Due to the computational resources needed to simulate quantum computers with a large number of qubits, we had to limit the study to systems with up to 12 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.
assertions.reader_inference: All results are therefore simulated small-scale results.

assertions.value: The authors state that exploring the actual implementability of the models on real hardware remains a possible extension of the analysis.
quotes: Moreover, one could explore the actual implementability of the models with real hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its scope.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no real-hardware experiment.

papers.title_in_file: The Quantum Path Kernel: a Generalized Quantum Neural Tangent Kernel for Deep Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, experiments, conclusion and appendix C. Appendix proofs skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation paper that defines the Quantum Path Kernel from the parameter trajectory of a quantum neural network and compares it with the Quantum NTK on Gaussian XOR mixtures.

assertions.value: The authors state that they show theoretically that the Quantum Path Kernel converges to the Quantum NTK only in the lazy training regime.
quotes: We have shown theoretically that the Quantum Path Kernel converges to the Quantum NTK only in the lazy training regime
assertions.certainty_reason: A theoretical result stated by the paper (proof not independently checked by the reader).

assertions.value: The authors report experimental results indicating superior generalization performance of the Quantum Path Kernel relative to the Quantum NTK, especially in high-depth, low signal-to-noise settings.
quotes: Experimental results indicate superior generalization performance relative to the Quantum NTK, an advantage which is especially pronounced in high-depth, low signal-to-noise settings.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulations on one synthetic benchmark.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that none of the simulated QNN models exhibit evidence of lazy training.
quotes: We can conclude that none of the QNN models exhibit evidence of lazy training.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one set of simulations.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments have not been run on quantum hardware.
assertions.anchor: Appendix C Data, Code, and Simulation details
quotes: These experiments have not been run on quantum hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.

papers.title_in_file: Resource Saving via Ensemble Techniques for Quantum Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, discussion, experiments I to IV results, resource-saving section and conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A study of bagging and AdaBoost ensembles of quantum neural networks, run in noiseless simulation, noisy simulation and on an IBM QPU.

assertions.value: The authors report that their experiments suggest a potential saving of 20% to 80% of the total qubit budget via the random subspace (attribute bagging) technique.
quotes: Our experiments (cf Figure 9) suggest a potential saving of 20% to 80% of the total qubit budget via this approach.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from a small set of datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that the effectiveness of bagging quantum models diminishes as the number of features decreases, so complex bagging models are still needed.
quotes: the effectiveness of bagging quantum models diminishes with a decrement in the number of features
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of a limit of its own method.

assertions.value: The authors state that one noisy experiment was run on the IBM Lagos QPU, a 7-qubit superconducting-based quantum computer, comparing the baseline model with a bagging configuration.
quotes: The second noisy experiment was performed directly on the IBM Lagos QPU real hardware. Such a device is a 7-qubit superconducting-based quantum computer.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The hardware experiment covers one synthetic regression task on a 7-qubit device.

assertions.value: The authors report in Experiment IV that all models except bagging with 30% of the features reach the same accuracy score of 97.2% at 10 layers.
quotes: all the models except bagging with 30% of the features achieve the same accuracy score of 97.2% using 10 layers
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated experiment.

papers.title_in_file: Kernel based quantum machine learning at record rate: Many-body distribution functionals as compact representations
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2303.16312v2 (26 May 2023). Here 'quantum machine learning' means classical kernel ridge regression models that predict quantum-chemistry properties of molecules. No quantum computer is used.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, kernel ridge regression section, timing results and conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A chemistry paper that introduces compact many-body distribution functional representations for kernel ridge regression on molecular properties (QM9, QMugs).

assertions.value: The authors report that on the QM9 dataset MBDF reaches a MAE of atomization energies of 0.69 kcal/mol after training on 32k molecules, using 5 dimensions to describe an atom.
quotes: On the QM9 dataset MBDF reaches a MAE of atomization energies of only 0.69 kcal/mol after training on 32k molecules while using only 5 dimensions to describe an atom.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that MBDF reduces the local kernel evaluation timings from days to a few minutes for both small and large molecules.
quotes: MBDF reduces the local kernel evaluation timings from days to a few minutes for both small and large molecules.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical timing result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the truncations used in this work may lead to lack of uniqueness of the representation, and that more rigorous numerical analysis would be desirable.
quotes: the truncations used in this work may lead to lack of uniqueness
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of a limit of its own method.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Transfer Learning with Adversarial Robustness for Classification of High-Resolution Image Datasets
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, circuit description, results (Tables I to IV discussion), discussion and conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of a quantum transfer learning model that attaches a variational quantum circuit to a classical network pre-trained on ImageNet, tested for accuracy and adversarial robustness.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Ants & Bees dataset the proposed QTL method achieves 96.1% accuracy while classical transfer learning reaches 94.7%.
quotes: For Ants & Bees dataset, the proposed method achieves 96.1% accuracy while the accuracy is 94.7% for classical TL.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum circuit uses six qubits to encode the six features output by the classical network.
quotes: we use six qubits as the input of the quantum circuit for encoding classical data with six features.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The reported results come from simulation, with the quantum part limited to six qubits.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum TL model is as vulnerable to adversarial attack as the classical TL method, and that adversarial training improved accuracy under attack.
quotes: the quantum TL model is as vulnerable to adversarial attack as the classical TL method
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulations on one dataset.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract claims the method is adversarially robust and outperforms classical methods; the results text reports equal vulnerability before adversarial training.

assertions.value: The authors state that applying quantum machine learning to large-scale high-resolution image datasets is not yet possible because of the limited number of qubits and the relatively high noise in current devices.
quotes: is not yet possible due to the limited number of qubits and relatively high level of noise in the current generation of quantum devices
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own motivation and scope.

papers.title_in_file: Representation Theory for Geometric Quantum Machine Learning
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2210.07980v2 (7 Feb 2023); the record id carries year 2023 and the file name 2022.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Sections II and III, and Section IX Outlook. The long representation theory sections were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A long tutorial that presents group and representation theory tools for geometric quantum machine learning.

assertions.value: The authors state that the article is not aimed at being a comprehensive review of representation theory; it presents basic group and representation theory tools through the lens of QML.
quotes: we note that this article is not aimed at being a comprehensive review of representation theory.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that they focus on the supervised QML problem of classifying labeled quantum data, and that the tools can broadly be used in unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning and generative modeling.
quotes: In this work we focus on the supervised QML problem of classifying labeled quantum data.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that the claim that models respecting dataset symmetries should perform better has been investigated and verified in the classical literature, but the same cannot be said for the quantum realm, where far more work is needed.
quotes: the same cannot be said for the quantum realm.
far more work is needed to elucidate problems wherein models with symmetry may be able to outperform symmetry-agnostic ones, possibly granting quantum advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the limits of current evidence.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Error Correction via Noise Guessing Decoding
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2208.02744v3 (27 Oct 2023); the record id carries year 2023 and the file name 2022.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusions and future directions, start of Appendix A. Derivations and simulations sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A quantum error correction paper that extends GRAND (guessing random additive noise decoding) to quantum random linear codes, giving a quantum-GRAND decoder.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is possible to both construct and decode QECCs that attain the maximum performance of the finite blocklength regime, for any chosen code length when the code rate is sufficiently high.
quotes: This paper shows that it is possible to both construct and decode QECCs that can attain the maximum performance of the finite blocklength regime, for any chosen code length when the code rate is sufficiently high.
assertions.certainty_reason: A headline claim of one paper; the reader did not check the derivations.

assertions.value: The authors state that numerical simulations first verified that the construction leading to random quantum codes can be efficiently implemented, even outside the regime with theoretical guarantees.
assertions.anchor: Section VIII Conclusions and Future Directions
quotes: It was first verified by numerical simulations that the construction leading to random quantum codes can be efficiently implemented, even outside the regime with theoretical guarantees.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work considers a system model with channel errors only, and that QECCs are considered mostly for quantum communications and quantum memories, not for errors during encoding and decoding in quantum computation.
assertions.anchor: Section VIII Conclusions and Future Directions
quotes: considering a system model with channel errors only, as a first extension of the GRAND concept to the quantum realm.
This work considered QECCs mostly for quantum communications and quantum memories, where the errors mostly arise during the quantum state transmission or storage.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope and limits.

assertions.value: The authors state that the application and efficiency of QGRAND for practical applications with limited qubit connectivity, and in the context of fault-tolerant systems, is the subject of ongoing work.
assertions.anchor: Section VIII Conclusions and Future Directions
quotes: The application and efficiency of QGRAND (and GRANDAB) for practical applications with limited qubit connectivity, and also in the context of fault-tolerant systems, is the subject of ongoing work.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of an open limit of its own work.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum neural networks form Gaussian processes
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2305.09957v3 (20 Nov 2024). The file name is truncated at the accented letter of the first author's surname.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, main results, Section III Discussion and Outlook. Supplementary proofs skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving that outputs of certain Haar random deep quantum neural networks converge to Gaussian processes in the limit of large Hilbert space dimension.

assertions.value: The paper proves that the output distribution of deep Haar random QNNs converges to a Gaussian process in the limit of large Hilbert space dimension, under certain conditions.
quotes: the output distribution of deep Haar random QNNs converges to a Gaussian process in the limit of large Hilbert space dimension.
assertions.certainty_reason: A proved result stated by the paper (proof not independently checked by the reader).

assertions.value: The authors state that their results are derived for QNNs that are Haar random over the unitary and orthogonal groups.
quotes: Our results are derived for QNNs that are Haar random over the unitary and orthogonal groups.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that Haar random QNNs will not necessarily always converge to a Gaussian process: not all QNNs and all measurements lead to one.
quotes: not all QNNs and all measurements will lead to a GP.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of the limits of its own result.
